nodes.title: Refine recording entry: hero-click starts, toolbar mic removed
nodes.body:
# Goal
Make the home hero **“Ready to record”** the start affordance for live meetings and remove the toolbar mic button (`ContentView.liveMeetingButton`).

Current state (verified):
- Hero card (`PreflightHomeView.header`) is a **status label** — dot + title + subtitle + a Re-check button; clicking it does nothing.
- Toolbar `.primaryAction` mic toggle is the only start entry outside the live pane (start when idle, stop while recording).
- The live pane (`LiveMeetingView`) already owns a Stop control and an idle “Start Recording” retry button.
- `PreflightOverall` gate exists (`fail` = “blocks recording if blocking”) but the toolbar button **bypasses it** — hero-as-entry can enforce it.

Decisions below, one per step.

nodes.title: D1 · Click target for starting
nodes.body:
What exactly becomes the record affordance in the hero card? (The card currently holds dot + verdict text + Re-check button — nested buttons are not allowed in SwiftUI, so this shapes the layout.)

**Recommendation: Option A.**

nodes.title: A · Left cluster is the button
nodes.body: Dot + “Ready to record” title + subtitle become one button; Re-check stays as its own control on the right. Matches your wording (“click on ‘ready to record’”), no nested-button surgery, Re-check untouched.

nodes.title: B · Dedicated Start Recording button
nodes.body: Add a prominent mic button (mic.fill, larger) beside Re-check; the verdict text stays a status label. Clearest affordance, but the click target is not the text you named.

nodes.title: C · Whole card clickable
nodes.body: Entire hero card is one button; Re-check must move out of the card (biggest layout change; where it goes is an open sub-question).

nodes.title: D2 · Verdict gating
nodes.body:
Which preflight verdicts may start a recording when clicked?

Current subtitles: `.unverified` = “You can record, but a run may fail”; `.blocked` = “Fix the failing check below before recording.”

**Recommendation: Option A** — it matches the existing copy exactly, and it finally enforces the `fail = blocks recording` gate that the toolbar button bypasses today.

nodes.title: A · .ready + .unverified start; .blocked inert
nodes.body: Green/amber hero clicks start the session; red (.blocked) renders non-interactive. Aligns UI with `PreflightOverall` semantics; blocked users are directed to the failing check instead of a doomed session.

nodes.title: B · Only .ready starts
nodes.body: Amber (.unverified) also inert. Stricter than the copy promises (“You can record”); forces a re-check loop for offline hiccups.

nodes.title: C · Blocked click reveals the issues
nodes.body: Red hero click expands the attention rows instead of recording. More magic in the card; attention rows are already shown above the fold when blocked.

nodes.title: D3 · Entry while a transcript is open
nodes.body:
Toolbar mic button is removed from **every** non-running phase, including `.document` (a transcript open). With it gone, starting a new live meeting while viewing a document requires clicking Home (chevron) first.

**Recommendation: Option A** — the toolbar removal is the point of the change; Home is one click away; a second document-phase affordance keeps two entry points alive.

nodes.title: A · Home is the only entry
nodes.body: Document phase keeps Share/Settings only. Single, discoverable entry point; simplest diff (toolbar group just loses one item).

nodes.title: B · Keep a record affordance in document view
nodes.body: e.g. a mic button in the document header row. Faster for the record-while-reading flow, but keeps a second entry point and contradicts “remove the top-right record button” in spirit.

nodes.title: D4 · Stop control while recording
nodes.body:
The toolbar button is currently the stop toggle while recording. With it gone, Stop lives only in the live pane header (`LiveMeetingView.stopControl`). After stop the model persists and opens the new transcript (existing behavior).

**Recommendation: Option A** — the pane control already exists and is the primary stop affordance; a second toolbar stop would recreate the removed control.

nodes.title: A · Pane-only stop
nodes.body: Live pane header Stop is the sole stop control. No toolbar changes beyond removing the start button.

nodes.title: B · Toolbar stop-only while recording
nodes.body: Keep a stop button in the toolbar only during `.recording/.stopping`. Two stop controls for one session; keeps a toolbar item that flickers in and out.

nodes.title: Refine the transcript + recording pages (2026-09-02)
nodes.body:
# Goal
Refine **both** pages — look and behaviour — now that the ground under them changed (light transcript = tinted paper, dark = the moving field, shipped `f81af11` today).

## The finding that shapes most of this
The live pane is supposed to *become* the document without the window changing. Measured, it does not:

| | Live (recording) | Finished (transcript) |
|---|---|---|
| body text | **14pt** | **18.5pt** |
| column | full window width | capped **34em ≈ 629pt**, centred |
| gutter | 52pt, mono 11pt | 48pt |
| speaker names | never (`speaker: nil`, RecordingPane.swift:764) | yes |
| timestamps | on every turn start | on hover only + moment pips |

So Stop swaps one reading surface for a very different one, in place.

Decisions below, one per step. Each carries a recommendation.

nodes.title: D1 · Do the two transcripts read alike?
nodes.body:
**Fact.** Live body is `.system(size: 14)` full-window-width. The finished document is 18.5pt inside a 34em (629pt) centred column. Same words, two surfaces, swapped at Stop.

**A.** Live adopts the document's column + 18.5pt body. One reading surface with two states; Stop stops being a visual event.
**B.** Live stays 14pt full width. A live feed is *scanned* for "is it hearing me", not read; a 629pt column in a 1400pt window wastes the room the meeting needs.

**Recommendation: A**, because the whole design argument for the recording pane is that it is the transcript arriving. If B, then say so in CLAUDE.md — the current text claims A and the code does B.

---
**RESOLVED 14:19 — A.** Live adopts the document's 34em centred column and 18.5pt body. The gutter comes to 48pt with it (one surface, one gutter). Stop ceases to be a visual event.

nodes.title: D2 · Nobody has a name during the meeting
nodes.body:
**Fact.** `LiveTranscriptLine.speaker` is hardcoded `nil` (RecordingPane.swift:764). The speaker row and the block grouping are built and never emitted. The engine is AssemblyAI **streaming v3** (`wss://streaming.assemblyai.com/v3/ws`), whose turn payload carries `transcript` + `endOfTurn` and **no speaker label** — so this is not waiting on plumbing, it is waiting on a capability the engine does not have.

**A.** Keep the empty row and wait (status quo). Costs nothing, ships nothing.
**B.** Label turns locally: run the existing ONNX d-vector embedder over each finalized turn's audio and match against enrolled voiceprints — the same pipeline `speakers.ts` already uses after the fact.

**Recommendation: B, but not now** — it is a feature (XIA-433-sized), not a refinement. Park it and say so, or the "speaker column" comment sits in the file another six months.

---
**RESOLVED 14:38 — B — build it.** Owner chose to BUILD live speaker naming (14:45). Architecture: ONE long-running node helper started with the session, loading the 27MB WeSpeaker ONNX once, taking a finalized turn's PCM on stdin and returning the best enrolled match. Rejected: spawn-per-turn (reloads 27MB every turn; names trail by seconds). Owed by the helper: start/health/kill on Stop, and no leak if the app quits mid-meeting. NOTE: live names are BEST-EFFORT — the seal still re-runs proper diarization + identification over the whole audio and is authoritative, so a live name may be corrected at Stop. AssemblyAI streaming v3 supplies no speaker labels at all, which is why this is embedding-side work and not a socket flag.

---
**RESOLVED 14:39 — B — build, names only.** Second half (14:47): live shows a name ONLY for a confident match (≥0.65) against an enrolled voiceprint. No on-the-fly 'Speaker 1/2' clustering — nothing on screen may be a guess. Consequence accepted: in a meeting where nobody is enrolled the live name column stays empty for the whole session; the seal still runs full diarization + identification and the finished document gets its labels there.

nodes.title: D3 · Scroll up mid-meeting and nothing tells you
nodes.body:
**Fact.** `isFollowing` is view `@State`. Scroll up → the newest line stops being chased. Nothing on screen says so, and the only way back is scrolling down within `followSlack` (24pt). Noted as an owner follow-up in the overnight run and never fixed.

**A.** A small "↓ newest" capsule appears in the cluster row only while follow is off; pressing it resumes. Says the state and is the way out of it — the Pause capsule's own rule (XIA-447).
**B.** Leave it. No control was deliberate: the volatile tail rewrites many times a second and a control invites fiddling.

**Recommendation: A.** The XIA-447 ruling — a state the owner cannot see is a state that reads as broken — applies exactly here.

---
**RESOLVED 14:28 — A.** A '↓ newest' pill fades in above the capsule row while follow is off, and pressing it scrolls to the newest line and resumes follow. Drawn as an OVERLAY (the moment tally's mechanism), never a fifth capsule — the row is centred and a fifth case would step Stop sideways under the pointer. Reduce Motion: the fade is kept, no movement.

nodes.title: D4 · The document header is a title and nothing else
nodes.body:
**Fact.** `DocumentHeaderView` draws `meta.title` alone. Date, duration, kind, speakers all live behind the Details button. The header cannot change height by construction (that fixed the shaking, XIA-441) — a *fixed* second line would not reintroduce it.

**A.** Keep title-only. The panel is the one place facts live; two places drift.
**B.** Restore one fixed subtitle line under the title — date + duration — because those two are what an owner scans to know *which* meeting this is, and opening a panel to learn that is a click for the most-asked question.

**Recommendation: B**, one line only, and `DocMeta.subtitle(facts:)` already exists and already drops the duplicated duration.

---
**RESOLVED 14:34 — B.** Owner's screenshot 14:28 overrode both original options. Settled: (a) the fixed header BAND goes entirely — the title becomes the first line of the scrolling document, in the reading column; (b) the '## Full Transcript' heading goes — the pane IS the transcript; (c) the pane draws title + transcript ONLY. Summary / Key Topics / Decisions / Action Items are dropped from the body — SummaryRailView already draws all four, so the pane was drawing them twice. Cost accepted: an imported .md with no record would lose its summary, so the panel falls back to parsing the markdown's own ## Summary when record == nil.

nodes.title: D5 · The Details panel holds six things
nodes.body:
**Fact.** `SummaryRailView` = subtitle + speaker chips + fact strip + tags + hairline + summary, in one scroll, ~890 lines. One amber dot on the button speaks for two unrelated claimants (a speaker suggestion, a stale summary).

**A.** Leave it. It was deliberately merged into one panel two weeks ago (ADR 0006) and splitting it re-opens a settled call.
**B.** Split: identity (chips + facts + tags) stays in the panel; the summary becomes its own surface, since it is the only half that is editable, spends money, and can fail.

**Recommendation: A.** ADR 0006 is three weeks old and the merge fixed real defects. If the panel feels crowded the cheaper fix is ordering and spacing inside it, not another surface.

---
**RESOLVED 14:39 — A.** Panel stays one panel (ADR 0006 upheld). Its stakes went UP with D4: the document body no longer draws the summary, so this panel is now the only home for narrative, key topics, decisions and action items. Any crowding is fixed by ordering and spacing inside it, never by a second surface. Follow-on owed by D4: the summary half must fall back to parsing the markdown's own '## Summary' when record == nil, or an imported .md loses its summary entirely.

nodes.title: D6 · Does the recording page wear paper in light mode too?
nodes.body:
**Fact.** `GroundPaper.wears(role:light:)` is `.transcript && light`. The recording page is `.recording` and so keeps the moving field in **both** themes. The transcribing screen is `.transcript` and wears paper.

So today: record on the field → stop → land on paper. Two different grounds either side of one press.

**A.** Recording keeps the field in light. It is not long-form reading; it is a live indicator surface and the field is what makes it feel alive.
**B.** Recording wears paper in light too, so the whole capture→read path is one surface.

**Recommendation: A**, and it is defensible: the measured lane rule (`three-lanes-for-text-on-colour`) is about **long-form reading**, and a live feed being scanned at 14pt is not that. But if D1 goes to A (live adopts the reading column) this flips — a 629pt reading column *is* long-form, and then B follows.

---
**RESOLVED 14:21 — B.** Recording wears paper in light too. Follows from D1: the live text is now long-form in a 629pt column, which the measured lane rule says may not sit on a pale multi-hue field. Dark is unchanged (field, push 0.97). CONSEQUENCE, decided not asked: recording and transcript wear the SAME paper — the transcript palette's — because two different tints either side of Stop is the visual event D1 and D6 both voted to remove. In light mode the recording palette therefore goes undrawn; home keeps its own field.

nodes.title: D7 · Timestamps say different things on each side
nodes.body:
**Fact.** Live draws a timestamp in a 52pt gutter at every turn start, always visible. The document shows nothing until hover (`HoverTimestampTextView`) and reserves its 48pt gutter for moment pips.

**A.** Live goes hover-only too, matching the document.
**B.** Keep both as they are: during a meeting "how long have we been talking" is live information; in a document it is reference you ask for.

**Recommendation: B.** Same content, different jobs — this is the one difference between the two surfaces that is earned. Worth writing down so a future consistency pass does not "fix" it.

---
**RESOLVED 14:27 — A.** Hover-only on both sides. The live gutter is still RESERVED at 48pt (hover timestamp + the ember marker rules live there) — it just draws nothing at rest, so no row steps left. Removes the last thing that changes at Stop.

nodes.title: D8 · BUG — the failure pill outlives its record
nodes.body:
**Reported by owner 14:28** ("check if this is true"), over a document holding a complete transcript. **It is true about a DIFFERENT recording.**

`NotaModel.backgroundFailure` (NotaModel.swift:987) is set in exactly one place — `finishBackgroundJob` (:1071), via `HandoffFailureNotice.message(status:hasRow:)`, which fires when a handed-off record failed and wrote no markdown (`hasRow: outputURL != nil`). It is cleared in exactly two: `startLiveSession` (:696) and the next `finishBackgroundJob` landing.

**Opening another document clears nothing.** So the pill is a window-level claim that survives navigation and sits over an unrelated, perfectly good transcript. `ContentView:108` renders it with no reference to what is on screen.

**Fix (no decision needed):** clear it when the open document changes. It says "the record you just handed off failed"; the moment the window is showing something else, it is no longer about anything visible.

**RESOLVED — fix as described.**

---
**RESOLVED 14:40 — fix as described.** No decision needed; fix is stated in the node.

nodes.title: D9 · Speaker names get their own column
nodes.body:
**Owner 14:28:** "verbatim and names should separate out. words should left align, names right align".

**Fact.** `MarkdownRender.appendSpeakerLine` draws `**Name:**` inline, in the speaker's identity hue, immediately before the words — so the text's left edge moves with the length of the name ("Brian Demsky:" vs "Freya Wu:") and the paragraph wraps back under the name.

**Target:** two columns. Names **right-aligned** in their own gutter; the words **left-aligned** on one shared edge, wrapping to that edge and never under the name.

Open sub-questions: how wide the name column is (fixed, or measured from the longest name in the document), and what happens when a name is longer than the column.

---
**RESOLVED 14:36 — measured + abbreviate.** Column is MEASURED per document from the longest speaker name, clamped to a max. Owner (14:41): a name over the cap is ABBREVIATED, never truncated. Ladder: full name → first name + last initial ('Brian D.') → initials ('B.D.') → ellipsis for a single over-long word. Full name always available on hover. Layout: outer 48pt gutter keeps the hover timestamps; the name column sits inside the text container as a right-aligned tab stop, with headIndent at the text edge so wrapped lines never run under a name.

nodes.title: Integration to-do (orchestrator only — lanes cannot be told)
nodes.body:
Carry-forward for the merge. None of these can be delegated: workflow lanes are
unreachable once running, and messaging one forks a second execution into its worktree
(learned the hard way at 14:52 today).

**1. The row cache will show a live name one turn late.** `LiveTranscriptRowCache.Key`
in `RecordingPane.swift` is (segmentCount, lastSegmentID, partial, elapsedSeconds,
markerSignature). A name is written **in place** onto an existing `segments[i].speaker`
and changes none of them, so the cache serves stale rows until the next turn bumps
`segmentCount`. Fix: a `speakerSignature` beside `markerSignature`. That file's own
comment already documents the identical failure for marker labels — the shape of the
fix is written down next to it. Reported by the helper-swift lane, which correctly
refused to edit a file it does not own.

**2. CLAUDE.md will conflict.** `lane/voiceprint-helper-swift` added 93 lines to
*The Recording Surface* (a new "Live speaker names" section plus a rewrite of the
now-false bullet claiming `LiveTranscriptLine.speaker` is nil and realtime labels are
an unresolved follow-up). `lane/live-reading-surface` is very likely editing the same
section. Two hunks, one localized resolve.

**3. Reconcile the two helper halves** against `docs/voiceprint-helper-protocol.md`
(commit 6c357a7), which is the declared authority. The Swift side confirms every
wire-shaped decision is a pure static on `VoiceprintHelperProcess` — `launchPlan`,
`requestLine`, `pcmBase64`, `name(fromAnswer:)`, `readiness(fromLine:)`, `lines(from:)`
— so absorbing a node-side divergence is those five functions and their tests, nothing
else. `NOTA_VOICEPRINT_HELPER` bridges a different entry point with no code change at all.

**4. Audit `bf4476e` for mixed authorship** — that worktree had two concurrent writers
for part of the run. CHECKED 15:08: five distinct top-level types, no duplicate
declarations, no semantic colours, 67 tests green on the final rebase. Clean.

---
**15:13 — item 3 resolved, and the authority is REVERSED.** The two halves diverge on
every line of the wire:

| | Swift | node |
|---|---|---|
| verb | `voiceprint serve` | `voiceprint-serve` (one command) |
| ready | `{"ready":true}` | `{"type":"ready","protocol":1,"ok":true,"speakers":2}` |
| request | `{"id":1,"sampleRate":16000,"pcm":…}` | `{"id":"7","op":"match","pcm":…}` |
| ok | `{"id":1,"name":…,"score":…}` | `{"id":"7","ok":true,"name":…,"score":…}` |
| fail | `{"id":1,"error":"insufficient_speech"}` | `{"id":"7","ok":false,…"insufficient-speech"}` |

**Adopt the NODE shape**, against what `docs/voiceprint-helper-protocol.md` says and
against what I told the Swift lane. Reasons: it carries a `protocol` version to bump,
an explicit `ok` discriminant rather than "an error key is present", and an `op` field
that leaves room for a second request type. Nothing is deployed, so there is no
compatibility to protect, and the Swift lane itself reported that every wire-shaped
decision is a pure static (`launchPlan`, `requestLine`, `pcmBase64`,
`name(fromAnswer:)`, `readiness(fromLine:)`, `lines(from:)`) — the cheapest surface in
the feature to move.

At integration: edit those six statics and their tests, change
`VoiceprintHelperProcess.verb` to `["voiceprint-serve"]`, and rewrite the pinned
protocol doc to describe what actually shipped. Do NOT edit either lane branch while
its reviewer is still reading it.

---
**15:40 — all seven lanes committed; sized the two known integration jobs.**

**Row cache: the blocker stands.** `LiveTranscriptRowCache.Key` on
`lane/live-reading-surface` is still (segmentCount, lastSegmentID, partial,
elapsedSeconds, markerSignature) — no speaker. That lane could not be told, as
expected. Fix at integration by adding a `speakerSignature` built exactly the way
`markerSignature` is; the comment justifying the marker one already argues the case
("`label` is a `var` the auto-title follow-up fills **in place**, and against a count
the transcript would then go on drawing the rows it built before the label existed").

**CLAUDE.md: four lanes edit it, but only ONE region truly conflicts.**

| lane | region | section |
|---|---|---|
| recording-wears-paper | ~1347–1400 | The Ground |
| document-surface | ~1487–1670 | The Document Surface |
| live-reading-surface | 1741, ~1969–2082 | The Recording Surface |
| voiceprint-helper-swift | ~2000–2008, 2272+ | The Recording Surface |

Only `live-reading-surface` and `voiceprint-helper-swift` both touch **line ~2000**.
Everything else is disjoint and only shifts offsets. So the merge is mechanical apart
from one paragraph, to be resolved by hand rather than by taking a side.
